questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Reinventing the wheel

options.text: Disturbing the system which has already been in use
Wasting one's time for things that have already been satisfactorily done
Examining circumstances that have already been understood

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Wasting one's time for things that have already been satisfactorily done'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom** 'Reinventing the wheel' **is **'Wasting one's time for things that have already been satisfactorily done'. (**उन चीजों के लिए अपना समय बर्बाद करना जो पहले ही संतोषजनक ढंग से की जा चुकी हैं**) **
 
• **Reinventing the wheel:** to waste time learning how to do something when it is already known how to do it
 
 
• Example: We don't need to **reinvent the wheel,** we just need to hire someone who already knows how to make the system work.</

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Nakul asked her, "How do you know that Rahul has told this to him?"

options.text: Nakul asked her how she knew that Rahul had told that to him.
Nakul asked her that how she has known that Rahul has told that to him.
Nakul asked her how she knew that Rahul has told that to him.
Nakul asked her that how she knows that Rahul had told that to him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Nakul asked her how she knew that Rahul had told that to him.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the question we have to change it into Indirect Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation as follows: 
 
 
• 'Asked' will not change because the given sentence is an 'Interrogative sentence'. 
 
• 'How' will be used as a conjunction because we know that in an interrogative sentence with a question word the question word itself is used as a conjunction. 
 
• **'You' **will be changed into** 'she' **because second-person pronouns are changed according to **the reporting verb** of the sentence in **'direct to indirect' **transformation. 
 
• We know that in the **'direct to indirect' **transformation **'First form' **of the verb is changed into **'Second form'** of **the verb. **
 
• **'Has told' **will be changed into** 'Had told'. **
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is** Option 1.** 

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__*** Nakul asked her how she knew that Rahul had told that to him.​ *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Transformation of Imperative Sentence:
 
 
• 'Orders', 'Command', 'Request', 'Advice' are given in these kinds of sentences. 
 
• Reporting Verb is changed into 'ordered, advised, requested, commanded, beg, forbade, suggested, proposed, assured, asked, reminded, warned, agreed, refused, promised', etc. 
 
• Inverted Commas will be removed. And conjunction 'to/not to' will be used. 
 
 
• *Example: *
 
 
• *He said, "John, please bring me my towel." (Direct Speech)*
 
• *He requested John to bring him his towel. (Indirect Speech)*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

This android can perform all the programmes perfectly well.

options.text: All the programmes can be performed perfectly well by this android.
All the programmes could have been performed perfectly well by this android.
All the programmes can have been performed perfectly well by this android.
All the programmes could be performed perfectly well by this android.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'All the programmes can be performed perfectly well by this android.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the** Active Voice.** As per the question we have to change it into **Passive Voice. **
 
• The process of transformation as follows:
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is** 'The android'.**
 
• The object of the given sentence is **'All the programmes'. **
 
• T**he structure of the transformation of Modals: **
 
 
• **Subject+Modals+V1+Object. (Active Voice)**
 
• **Subject(objective case)+Modals+be+V3+by+object(subjective case). (Passive Voice)**
 
 
 
• *Example: *
 
 
• *Animals cannot make tools. (Active Voice)*
 
• *Tools cannot be made by animals. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• We know that in **Active To Passive** transformation** 'can perform'** will be changed into** 'can be performed'. ** 
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 1. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *All the programmes can be performed perfectly well by this android. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Transformation of Infinitives: Structure of it as follows:

__
 
• Subject+is/am/are/was/were/has/have/had+to+V1+Object. 
 
• Subject(Objective case)+is/am/are/was/were/has/have/had+to+be+V3+by+object(subjective case). 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Your child is to learn chess. (Active Voice)*
 
• *Chess is to be learnt by your child. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__***We do not change the tense of a verb when we convert a sentence from the active to the passive voice or vice versa.***__

questions.question:
**Given below are four Jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. He was on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem.

B. The villagers were kind though doubtful.

C. They offered him some food to eat and a room to stay.

D. One night, he took rest in a village unfamiliar on the way.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'ADBC'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble. 
 
• The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
• Here, in the given question **Part A** will be the **first** sentence because it is the starting of an incident. 
 
• **Part D** will be the next sentence because **Part A **talks about the pilgrimage of the person. And **Part D** tells us where he took shelter. 
 
• Part B will be the next because it describes the behavior of Villagers. 
 
• Lastly, **Part C** will be used because **Part C** tells us how Villagers treated him. 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 3. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *He was on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem. One night, he took rest in a village unfamiliar on the way. The villagers were kind though doubtful. They offered him some food to eat and a room to stay.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No improvement'.**

She is tender-hearted by nature and I have found her eyes moist __many a times__ over the sad face of any children.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'many a time'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• The idiom **'many a time' **means **'many times'.** 
 
 
• *Example: I've told you **many a time** not to ride your bike on the pavement.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 4. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *She is tender-hearted by nature and I have found her eyes moist **many a time** over the sad face of any children. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__** 

 
• We tend to go for Option 3 but it would be wrong because **"A"** is a **singular indefinite article**, and** "times"** is plural.
 
• The two do not mix, therefore, it is wrong. **"Many a times"** may be **a colloquialism**, but it is still incorrect.
 
• **"Many a time"** and **"many times"** mean the same thing, but** "many a time" **is a more formal or old-fashioned way to say **"many times".**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

• Here, in the given question the main subject is **'the issues'.** And it is in the plural form. 
 
• Hence, a plural auxiliary verb **'have'** should be used instead of **'has'.**
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 2. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *Some of the issues discussed in the media nowadays **have no relevance** to the nation-building process.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. The driver had a cloudy look drove off without taking him.

B. He asked a taxi driver to take him to the shopping mall.

C. He told the driver that he could pay the fare by card, not in cash.

D. He arrived on the outskirts of a city.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'DBCA'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble. 
 
• The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
 
• Here, in the given question the first sentence will be** 'Part D'.** Because** Part D **is the starting of an incident that is* 'arrival of someone at the outskirts of a city'. *
 
• **Part B** will be the next sentence because after arrival **'He'** took a **'taxi driver'**. 
 
• **Part C** will be the next sentence because **Part B** is connected with **Part C.** It tells us what that person told **'Driver'. **
 
• And lastly, **Part A **will be the last sentence because it tells how the driver reacted. 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 1. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *He arrived on the outskirts of a city. He asked a taxi driver to take him to the shopping mall. The driver had a cloudy look drove off without taking him. The driver had a cloudy look drove off without taking him.*
